data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in New Zealand performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably comparing 2018 vs 2022 and trends back to 2012 and earlier). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2 baseline and Level 5/6 top performers), and gaps by student characteristics such as socioeconomic status (ESCS), gender, and immigrant background, alongside contextual indicators from student and school questionnaires (e.g., belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences). The document also flags that New Zealand’s response rates fell below PISA technical targets, and that an analysis suggests reported mean scores may be higher by about 10 points than hypothetical means including non-respondents. Because this is a descriptive reporting product (not an ML study), no predictive model metrics, algorithmic methods, or explicit PV/missing-data handling procedures are provided.
